title: The Real Cost of Prop Firm Resets: Do the Math Before You Buy Another One
excerpt: Resets feel cheap one at a time. Added up over a year, they're often the biggest line in a trader's budget. A simple way to calculate your real cost per funded account and decide when to stop and fix the process first.
seoTitle: Prop Firm Reset Cost: How Much Are Resets Really Costing You? (2026)
seoDescription: Calculate what prop firm resets and evaluation fees really cost you per year and per funded account, and use a simple rule to decide when to stop buying resets and fix your process.
keywords: is a prop firm reset worth it
author: Zentrade Team
thumbnailAlt: Trader reviewing the cost of prop firm evaluations and resets

content.text: The real cost of prop firm resets is the number of resets you bought in a year multiplied by what each one cost, plus every evaluation fee. Divide that total by the number of funded accounts you actually got and you have your cost per funded account. For many traders, that number is much higher than they'd guess, because each reset was bought on its own, usually right after a bad day.

Reset and evaluation prices change often and vary by firm, account size and promotion, so this article uses your own numbers instead of quoting firm prices. Pull them from your email receipts or your card statement.
Step 1: Count What You Actually Spent

items: Search your email for receipts from each firm over the last 12 months.
List every evaluation purchase, reset, and monthly fee separately.
Add activation or data fees if your firm charges them.
Add it all up. Don't round down.

content.text: Or use the reset calculator on our homepage: enter the resets you paid and what you paid for each.

Cost per funded account = Total spent ÷ Funded accounts obtained. If you haven't been funded yet, the honest answer is that the number is still growing. The table below uses illustrative prices, not any firm's actual prices.

Getting funded isn't the finish line either. Funded accounts have their own rules for drawdown, consistency and payouts. A funded account that's lost a week later doesn't pay back the resets that came before it.
Step 3: Find Out Why Each Attempt Ended
The cost is a symptom. The cause is in how each attempt ended. For each failed evaluation, write one line: which rule was broken, and what happened in the hour before.

rows: Trailing drawdown hit after a winning streak
Size didn't shrink as the floor moved up
Kept trading after the first losses
Personal daily limit below the firm's
Big loss right after a loss
Track best day as % of profit
Forcing trades to hit the target
Trade cap and planned setups only

content.text: A Simple Rule: When to Stop Buying Resets

If your last two attempts ended the same way, don't buy a third reset yet. Spend one or two weeks trading the same plan on a simulator or a small personal account and log every trade. Buy the next evaluation when you have two clean weeks: daily limit respected every day and no trades after hitting it. That's a process threshold, not a guarantee. Nothing guarantees passing an evaluation, but repeating the same failure for another fee doesn't change the odds.
Treat Evaluations as a Budget, Not an Impulse

items: Set a monthly evaluation budget before the month starts, and don't top it up after a bad day.
Never buy a reset the same day you failed. That's the same emotional state that caused the failure.
Wait for discounts only if your process is ready. A cheap reset on a broken process is still money lost.
Track the total, not the individual price. Individual resets always look small.

faqItems.q: Is a prop firm reset worth it?
faqItems.a: Only if you know why the last attempt ended and you've changed something. If your last two attempts failed the same way, fix the process first, because another reset on the same process is likely to end the same way.

faqItems.q: How do I calculate what resets cost me?
faqItems.a: Add every evaluation fee, reset and recurring fee from the last 12 months, then divide by the number of funded accounts you obtained. That's your cost per funded account.

faqItems.q: How many resets does it take to pass a prop firm evaluation?
faqItems.a: There's no reliable number. Firms publish different pass-rate statistics, and they depend on how attempts are counted. What you can control is not repeating the same failure.

faqItems.q: Should I buy a reset right after failing?
faqItems.a: It's better to wait at least a day and review what happened first. Buying immediately after a failure is often the same emotional decision that caused it.
